## Reset Consistency Checker

### Overview

This module checks the behavior of one leaf reset in the reset distribution network. Its purpose is to verify that the leaf reset asserts only when it has a legitimate cause. A legitimate cause is either:

- the parent reset asserting, or
- a software reset request asserting.

The module also verifies that the parent and leaf resets assert and release in the expected order. If an inconsistency is detected, the module reports a fatal error.

### Interface Behavior

The module has the following externally observable behavior:

- A local clock, used to perform all checking operations.
- A local reset, used to place the checker into its initial inactive state.
- A child clock, associated with the leaf reset domain being checked.
- A parent reset input, representing the upstream reset that should cause the leaf reset.
- A child reset input, representing the leaf reset being checked.
- A software reset request input, representing a software-requested reset cause.
- A software reset request clear output, used to clear a pending software reset request.
- An error output, asserted when a reset consistency violation is detected.

In this document, “asserted” means the reset is active. For an active-low reset, this is the low level.

### Initialization

When the local reset is asserted, the error output shall be deasserted and the checker shall not perform any consistency checks.

After the local reset is released, the checker shall remain inactive until both the parent reset and the child reset have been observed deasserted. This prevents ambiguous conditions at startup from being treated as consistency errors.

### Reset Assertion Checking

Once the checker is initialized, the following rules shall apply.

- If the child reset asserts while the parent reset is asserted, the child reset assertion is valid.
- If the child reset asserts while the software reset request is asserted, the child reset assertion is valid, even if the parent reset is not asserted.
- If the child reset asserts while neither the parent reset nor the software reset request is asserted, the checker shall wait for the parent reset to assert. This wait shall be bounded by the configured timeout. If the parent reset does not assert within that timeout, the checker shall assert the error output.
- A software reset request that appears after the child reset has already been observed asserting without any source shall not validate the child reset assertion. In that situation, the checker shall still require the parent reset to appear within the timeout.
- If the parent reset asserts while the child reset is not asserted, the checker shall wait for the child reset to assert. This wait shall also be bounded by the configured timeout. If the child reset does not assert within that timeout, the checker shall assert the error output.
- A software reset request alone, without a child reset assertion, shall not cause any check or error.

### Release Checking

After a child reset assertion has been accepted as valid, the checker shall wait for the cause of the assertion to be released before expecting the child reset to release.

The cause is considered present when the parent reset is asserted or the software reset request is asserted. The cause is considered released only when both are deasserted.

During this waiting period:

- The checker shall assert the software reset request clear output, so that any pending software reset request can be cleared.
- If the child reset releases while the cause is still present, the checker shall assert the error output, because the child reset released before its cause.
- The checker shall wait indefinitely for the cause to release; the configured timeout does not apply to this wait.

After the cause has been released, the checker shall wait for the child reset to release.

During this child-release wait:

- The timeout shall be measured only when child clock activity is observed. This prevents a slow or stopped child clock from causing a false timeout. If no child clock activity occurs, the timeout shall not expire.
- If the child reset remains asserted for longer than the configured timeout, measured in child clock activity, the checker shall assert the error output.
- If the parent reset or software reset request re-asserts before the child reset releases, the checker shall return to waiting for the cause to be released.
- If the child reset releases, the checker shall return to normal monitoring.

### Error Behavior

The error output shall be asserted whenever any consistency violation described above is detected. Once asserted, it shall remain asserted until the local reset is cycled. No other input shall clear the error output.

The checker shall not generate, modify, or otherwise drive any reset signal. It only monitors reset behavior and reports inconsistencies.

### Timeout Configuration

The checker shall be parameterized with a maximum synchronization delay. This parameter shall define:

- the maximum time to wait for a missing parent reset after a child reset assertion,
- the maximum time to wait for a missing child reset after a parent reset assertion,
- the maximum child-clock-activity time to wait for a child reset release after the cause has been released.

# Behavioral Specification: Leaf Reset Generator

## 1. Overview

This module generates one active-low leaf reset for a downstream logic domain and checks that every assertion of that reset is justified.

The leaf reset must be asserted whenever:

- the parent reset is asserted, or
- a software reset request is asserted or has been latched, or
- scan mode is active and the scan reset is asserted.

The module also provides an encoded indication of whether the leaf reset is currently asserted, and an error indication used to report unjustified reset assertions.

## 2. Reset Output Behavior

### 2.1 Functional Mode

In normal functional operation, the leaf reset output has the following behavior:

- Reset asserted means logic `0`.
- Reset deasserted means logic `1`.
- The output must be asserted when the parent reset is asserted.
- The output must be asserted when a software reset request is present.
- The output must remain asserted while either of those conditions remains true.
- The output must deassert only when no reset request is active and no parent reset is asserted.
- The output must be glitch-free when entering or leaving the reset state.

### 2.2 Parent Reset

The parent reset is the upstream reset in the reset cascade.

When the parent reset asserts, the leaf reset must assert regardless of the state of the software reset request.

The leaf reset must remain asserted until the parent reset deasserts and there is no software reset request still pending or active.

### 2.3 Software Reset Request

The software reset request is active-low. A request is considered asserted when the active-low request input is `0`.

The module must latch a software reset request when it is asserted.

Once latched, the request must remain active at the reset consistency checker even if the original software request deasserts. This ensures that the checker can identify the cause of a short software-requested reset. The physical leaf reset follows the synchronized original software request and the parent reset.

The latched software request may be cleared only after the reset consistency check confirms that the leaf reset assertion is justified.

If the original software request remains asserted after the latched request is cleared, the leaf reset must continue to be asserted until the software request is removed.

### 2.4 Scan Mode

When scan mode is selected, the normal functional reset generation path is bypassed.

In scan mode:

- The leaf reset output must follow the scan reset input.
- The parent reset and software reset request must not directly control the reset output.
- If the scan reset is asserted, the leaf reset must be asserted.
- If the scan reset is deasserted, the leaf reset must be deasserted.

The output reset state in scan mode is still the final reset state observed by the consistency check and by the reset-asserted indication.

## 3. Reset Consistency Checking

Every leaf reset assertion must be checked to verify that it has a valid cause.

A leaf reset assertion is valid if either:

- the parent reset is asserted, or
- a software reset request is present, including a latched software request.

The module must tolerate skew between the leaf reset assertion and the parent reset or software request indication. The parent reset and the leaf reset may be observed in either order. The module must wait for the matching conditions to be observed before declaring the reset valid.

If a leaf reset asserts and no parent reset or software request is observed within a bounded synchronization timeout, the module must assert the error output.

The error output must not assert during a normal parent reset or software reset sequence.

Once the consistency check confirms that the leaf reset assertion is valid, any latched software request may be cleared, and the normal reset release behavior may complete.

## 4. Reset-Asserted Indication

The module must provide an encoded status indication that reports whether the leaf reset is currently asserted.

This indication must be based on the final leaf reset output, including scan mode selection.

- When the leaf reset is asserted, the indication must carry the value meaning “true”.
- When the leaf reset is deasserted, the indication must carry the value meaning “false”.

The indication must be valid during reset assertion and must update correctly when the leaf reset is released.

## 5. Error Output Behavior

The error output is inactive during normal reset operation.

The error output must assert if the leaf reset is observed asserting without a valid parent reset or software reset request cause within the allowed synchronization timeout.

The error output is an indication only; it does not itself control the leaf reset output. The leaf reset output continues to be controlled by the parent reset, software reset request, and scan mode selection.

## 6. Summary of Required Behavior

| Condition | Leaf Reset Output | Consistency Error |
|---|---|---|
| Parent reset asserted | Asserted | Not asserted |
| Software reset request asserted or latched | Asserted | Not asserted |
| Neither parent reset nor software request active | Deasserted | Not asserted |
| Scan mode active, scan reset asserted | Asserted | Valid if parent/request justification present |
| Scan mode active, scan reset deasserted | Deasserted | Not asserted |
| Leaf reset asserted with no observed justification | Asserted | Asserted after timeout |

The module must implement these behaviors without relying on any particular ordering between the parent reset and leaf reset assertion, and without releasing a latched software reset request before the reset consistency check has completed.
